transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Product), Sarah O'Connor (NovaMed CTO), Ravi Shah (Platform Eng), Emily Tan (Security), Noah Li (Data Scientist)

Topics: Model catalog demo, selecting open models, benchmarks, compatibility matrices, hosted vs dedicated, VPC/KMS, SOC2

[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll hand over to Priya to kick off the model catalog walkthrough, we've got Carlos on product too
[00:12] Priya: thanks Jordan, hi Sarah, hi team, quick agenda  show you the model catalog UI in Console, how we select open model variants, show perf benchmarks and the compatibility matrix, then Q&A and next steps
[00:30] Sarah: sounds good, we have 45 minutes, we mainly want to understand latency + cost for our EHR summarization flows and security posture
[00:40] Priya: perfect. quick context question  what's your typical prompt length and concurrency?
[00:50] Ravi: most prompts are 400-1200 tokens, but we also have some clinical note gen bursts that can go to 6k+ tokens. concurrency is moderate, around 40 concurrent inference streams during peak
[01:05] Priya: good to know, that's why we'll show both trimmed and long-seq profiles  our catalog has open models and tuned profiles like 4k and 8k sequence configs
[01:20] Carlos: one thing to call out, the catalog pairs each model with a performance profile that includes latency P50/P99, memory footprints, and recommended quantization. compatibility matrix shows which runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private) and which hardware (A100, H100, RTX-class) are supported
[01:40] Noah: are the quantized variants functionally equivalent? we worry about hallucination/regression
[01:47] Priya: good question, quantization can introduce small quality shifts. in the UI we surface eval scores vs a golden prompt set, you can click to see delta for ROUGE/BLEU or custom metrics. we recommend running your prompt set through our Optimize tooling to get concrete regressions
[02:05] Sarah: can you show the actual compatibility matrix?
[02:09] Priya: sure, switching to Console, this is the Model Catalog page  left column is model family, middle is variants (fp16, int8-q4), right is compatibility matrix. for example, open-llama-13b-int8 is supported on hosted, dedicated on RTX and A100, but for private on-prem we currently support A100/H100 only
[02:35] Emily: quick security question, does hosted option ever see customer data unencrypted? we need end-to-end encryption and KMS integration
[02:43] Jordan: short answer: we offer encryption at rest and in transit by default, we support customer-managed KMS keys for private deployments and Dedicated via KMS integrations; hosted API can be configured with client-side encryption for sensitive payloads. we'll share the security whitepaper and the KMS integration guide
[03:05] Emily: ok please share the docs
[03:09] Jordan: noted  we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs and the KMS guide after the call (link in follow-up)
[03:18] Priya: back to compatibility  matrix also shows feature flags like streaming, function-calling, and whether KV-cache prefixing is available. there are some caveats: very long sequences can require different kernel paths and may not support the smallest GPU targets
[03:35] Ravi: you mentioned kernel selection  how automated is that? we don't want to manage low-level tuning
[03:40] Priya: it's automated; runtime profiles include kernel selection heuristics based on seq length dist and model arch. we also provide recommended quant and batch sizes in Optimize tab
[03:50] Carlos: i'll add that for customers we can provide a tailored quantization recommendation based on a sample prompt set to maintain quality targets
[04:05] Noah: on benchmarking  what's included in the perf numbers? are these cold-starts or steady-state?
[04:12] Priya: our reported P50/P99 are steady-state with our continuous batching enabled; we provide separate cold-start numbers. the benchmark sheet we share includes token/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and tail latency for different seq lengths and hardware
[04:30] Sarah: can you run a benchmark with our prompt set? we need to validate quality and p99 latency at 4k seq
[04:36] Priya: yes  action item: we'll run a short benchmark with your prompt set on an 8k-profile to capture worst-case tails, also include an 800-token profile for typical workloads
[04:48] Jordan: attaching the sample benchmark template and a shared spreadsheet in chat (link)
[04:55] Priya: now demoing the bench UI  you can filter by model family, hardware, seq len. here's an example: open-model-x-30b fp16 on A100 P50 85ms token, P99 420ms at 512 token workload, cost estimates shown per 1k tokens
[05:20] Ravi: ok numbers look reasonable; how do we interpret cost vs latency? can we set routing policy to prefer cheaper variants unless latency SLO breached?
[05:28] Priya: yes, Smart Routing. you can set route policies by latency SLO, cost budget, region. policies can fallback to lower-cost variants or to a cached KV prefix. we also support canary rollouts so you can test variants gradually
[05:45] Sarah: for our regulated workloads we prefer predictable latency  we might go Dedicated for certain routes. what's the pricing delta and lead time for Dedicated?
[05:55] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity; pricing is a monthly commit and we can provide a pilot committed pack. typical lead time for GPU provisioning depends on region but we can usually do a pilot in 24 weeks; finance will follow up with exact quotes
[06:15] Emily: for Dedicated, is customer data isolated and do you support VPC peering?
[06:20] Jordan: yes Dedicated is single-tenant pools with VPC peering options and audit logs; we support SAML SSO and RBAC at token-level
[06:30] Priya: switching to Optimize  this is the recommendation engine: it analyzes token distribution, suggests batching thresholds, cache TTLs, and quant profiles to hit a cost target while keeping quality. here's an example recommendation: for your dataset we recommend int8 q4 on RTX for 90% of requests and fp16 for long clinical note gen routes
[06:55] Noah: will that recommendation include sample prompts where quality regresses?
[07:00] Priya: yes, Optimize shows per-prompt deltas and flags regressions above threshold; you can define custom evals and set alerts for quality regressions after changes
[07:12] Sarah: we also need auditing  can you store inference inputs/outputs for X days and tie to audit logs?
[07:20] Jordan: yes retention is configurable; for hosted we have a default retention policy but you can extend retention in Enterprise plans; all logging is integrated into the Console with export to your SIEM
[07:32] Ravi: about the compatibility matrix  any gotchas for LLMs with large KV caches? we use prefix caching extensively
[07:38] Priya: prefix/KV caches are supported; caveat is memory footprint increases with long prefix state so some smaller GPUs might not be able to keep very large caches  the matrix flags those combos and suggests sharding or dedicated pool configs
[07:55] Carlos: also note that for private/on-prem we have additional constraints around library versions; sometimes you need a specific CUDA/driver combo; we document that per-variant in the matrix
[08:10] Emily: what's the upgrade story for models? we want deterministic rollouts and rollback in case of regressions
[08:18] Priya: in Console you can pin model versions per route, we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback if quality alerts trigger. rollout configs include percent traffic, time windows, and automatic fallback to a pinned baseline
[08:33] Noah: will we be able to run local evals in our CI? integrate with your API?
[08:38] Priya: yes, Optimize exposes an API and SDK to run evals in CI; you can push eval results into our quality dashboards
[08:45] Sarah: any customers with similar compliance needs in healthcare?
[08:50] Jordan: yes, a few providers use Private + Dedicated combos; we can share redacted case studies and reference architecture  will include in follow-up
[09:00] Priya: demoing filtering in the catalog: you can filter by tokenization (bpe vs sentencepiece), supported features, and measured eval deltas. click into a model and it shows sample prompts, evals, kernel recommendations, and infra compatibility
[09:20] Ravi: the sample prompts  are those editable? can we attach our canonical prompts?
[09:25] Priya: absolutely, you can upload custom prompt sets for Optimize to analyze, and those are used to produce the bench runs and delta reports
[09:33] Carlos: quick note: be aware that open model naming in transcriptions sometimes get munged  the Console shows canonical model IDs you should reference in infra configs
[09:45] Sarah: ok one more question on latency SLOs  can you enforce per-route P99 with automatic spilling?
[09:50] Priya: yes, you can set SLO-based routing  if P99 approaches threshold traffic can spill to a higher-tier variant or dedicated pool; we also support circuit-breakers to protect downstream systems
[10:05] Noah: how do you measure tokenization differences across models for cost predictions? tokenization can seriously change cost
[10:12] Priya: Optimize computes tokenization on your prompt set across candidate models and shows per-model token counts and resulting cost estimates  that's why we always recommend running your prompt set, not generic benchmarks
[10:25] Sarah: ok that answers a lot. can we talk briefly about data residency? some patient data must remain in-region
[10:32] Jordan: we have region controls for Hosted and Dedicated  for private on-prem obviously you control residency. we'll include region options in the pricing doc
[10:40] Emily: auditing again  how long do you keep audit logs and are they immutable?
[10:45] Jordan: audit logs are append-only and can be exported to your S3 with object lock for immutability if you require it
[10:55] Priya: jumping to practical step: i'm going to run a targeted bench on a small subset of your prompts to show P50/P99 and cost  quick confirmation: which model family do you want to try first? we can try open-llama-13b-int8 and an fp16 variant for baseline
[11:15] Ravi: let's do open-llama-13b-int8 and a 30b fp16 baseline, that should show tradeoffs
[11:22] Priya: great. i'll schedule the bench now  we'll run two profiles: 800-token typical and 4k/8k worst-case. results will include per-prompt deltas and tokenization counts
[11:35] Noah: curious  if a quantized variant regresses on a few prompts can you route those prompts to fp16 only?
[11:41] Priya: yes you can set per-prompt or per-route overrides in routing rules. Optimize can also suggest which prompts to route differently based on eval deltas
[11:50] Sarah: timeline wise, we want to make a pilot decision in two weeks, and a production plan in a month
[11:56] Jordan: understood  we'll prioritize the bench and security docs for immediate next steps
[12:05] Priya: any other technical concerns?
[12:08] Emily: one last on HSM  does Redwood support customer-managed HSM for key wrapping?
[12:14] Jordan: yes, HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we support customer-managed KMS keys via cloud provider integrations. we'll include the integration guide
[12:25] Priya: ok demo wrap-up  recap: we showed catalog UI, compatibility matrix, Optimize recommendations, and routing features. next: we'll run bench, share matrix and security pack, and schedule a follow-up on pricing
[12:40] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links; expecting to follow-up with bench results and docs by next week
[12:48] Sarah: thanks all, appreciate the walkthrough
[12:52] Meeting ends

Notes about transcription: occasional transcription artifacts (model names spelled inconsistently, e.g., open-llama vs openlama), some technical terms split (K V cache), filler words and crosstalk present. Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://drive.google.com/bench-novamed), security packet (link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-novamed)
